title: Skeleton-Guided Progressive Test-Time Adaptation for Thin Curvilinear Structures (SGP-TTA)
mechanism: Consensus Skeleton Recall builds a skeleton target from 6 aligned views and updates only the BN affine parameters (1 step per image); ProgBN moves BN statistics from source toward target by sample count.
adaptation: Drop ProgBN, because our BN-statistics TTA failed (T9, BN-HC). Keep CSR on BN affine only. Adapt continually within one E1 module and reset between modules; adapt episodically per cell on test. Skeleton dilation r=2 matches our 2 px label jitter. It extends our training-time Skeleton Recall w0.1, which was a narrow E1 pass.
min_experiment: Arm: SUP100-PF + CSR (lr chosen on F51 from 1e-4 to 1e-3, 6 views, dilation 2). Baseline: SUP100-PF without TTA. Metrics: E1 relF1@2 and component recall, with test clean-49 crack IoU as a guard. Kill if E1 relF1@2 gains < +0.02, or test crack IoU or mIoU_rob drops > 0.005, or H36 crack-free false alarms rise > 2x.
evidence: R (full text): UNet at 512 px on 10 curvilinear datasets. DRIVE to STARE Dice: source 51.3, TENT 71.0, SGP 74.2. When the source model is already good (CNDS 85.56), TENT, CoTTA, SAR and EATA fall to 62 to 63 while SGP holds 85.27. Adding entropy hurt (65.22 to 62.36 retina; 59.15 to 44.98 road). Plain multi-view consistency alone was tiny (53.51 to 53.93).
prior_overlap: The ProgBN part overlaps T9 / BN-HC (per-panel and global BN statistics failed under the same conditions), so it is dropped. CSR on BN affine at test time was never run, so it is open.
